title: SSL/TLS inspection rule criteria and the ones that silently don't match

prose.text: "Why didn't this SSL rule match?" can be a criterion that was ignored or cannot be evaluated for this traffic. Start with the expression. {{operator-expression}} {{second-dimension-narrows}} {{zcc-criteria-unset-ignored}}

prose.label: Criteria that need a careful reading.

items.label: Destinations.
items.text: {{destination-group-types}} {{dest-ip-groups-ignored-with-sni}} Whether a rule scoped only by IP destination groups then matches every request with SNI or none of them is not documented {{gap:ip-dest-group-ignored-effect}}.

items.label: ZPA.
items.text: {{zpa-segments-sipa-only}} The criterion has no counterpart on URL Filtering or Cloud App Control rules {{gap:absent-from-url-filtering-and-cac}}.

prose.label: Identity.
prose.text: {{identity-needs-zcc-or-surrogate-ip}} This is the same constraint as the first pass in [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]], which is evaluated before decryption on the CONNECT or SNI alone.

How the matching rule is chosen is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.rules]]; what it then does is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.actions]]. The URL Filtering criteria tree is a different expression with different fields: [[zia.url-filtering.criteria]].

checks.do: Whether a criterion in the rule's expression is ignored or cannot be evaluated for this traffic, starting from the operator expression.
Which destination type to scope an SSL rule by: FQDN groups, URL categories or cloud applications rather than IP groups, unless the target has no SNI.

operator-expression.statement: An SSL/TLS inspection rule matches when this expression is true: Source IP Groups AND [URL Categories OR Cloud Applications OR Destination Groups OR Forwarding Gateways] AND ZPA Application Segment AND [Location Groups OR Locations] AND [Users OR Groups OR Departments] AND [Device Groups OR Devices OR Remote Users with Kerberos] AND Device Trust Level AND User Agent AND [Endpoint Applications OR Endpoint Application Tags] AND Endpoint Application Risk Level.

quotes: Source IP Groups (AND) [URL Categories (OR) Cloud Applications (OR) Destination Groups (OR) Forwarding Gateways] (AND) ZPA Application Segment (AND)
[Location Groups (OR) Locations] (AND) [Users (OR) Groups (OR) Departments] (AND) [Device Groups (OR) Devices (OR) Remote Users with Kerberos] (AND) Device Trust Level (AND) User Agent (AND)
[Endpoint Applications (OR) Endpoint Application Tags] (AND) Endpoint Application Risk Level.

operator-expression.conditions: Corrected on recapture (2026-10-18): previously "An SSL/TLS inspection rule matches when this expression is true: Source IP Groups AND [URL Categories OR Cloud Applications OR Destination Groups OR Forwarding Gateways] AND ZPA Application Segment AND [Location Groups OR Locations] AND [Users OR Groups OR Departments] AND [Device Groups OR Devices OR Remote Users with Kerberos] AND Device Trust Level AND CONNECT User-Agent."

zcc-criteria-unset-ignored.statement: Device trust levels, device groups and devices are documented as applicable to devices managed by Client Connector, and when none is set the criterion is ignored during evaluation; an unset `platforms` list means the rule applies to all device platforms.

quotes: This field is applicable for devices that are managed using Zscaler Client Connector. If no value is set, this field is ignored during the policy evaluation.
Specifies devices that are managed using Zscaler Client Connector. If no value is set, this field is ignored during the policy evaluation.
List of device trust levels for which the rule must be applied. This field is applicable for devices that are managed using Zscaler Client Connector.
If no value is set, this field is ignored during the policy evaluation. DeviceTrustLevels []string
If no value is set, this field is ignored during the policy evaluation. DeviceGroups []common.IDNameExtensions
If no value is set, this field is ignored during the policy evaluation. Devices []common.IDNameExtensions

expect.description: Zscaler Client Connector device platforms for which the rule must be applied. If not set, rule is applied to all device platforms

evidence.note: platforms: 'If not set, rule is applied to all device platforms'

dest-ip-groups-ignored-with-sni.statement: IP address-based destination groups in a rule's criteria are ignored during policy evaluation when the HTTPS request carries an SNI value.
dest-ip-groups-ignored-with-sni.conditions: The second half of the statement (matches only requests without SNI) follows from the quoted rule; the help page does not spell it out.

quotes: During policy evaluation, IP address-based destination groups in the rule criteria are ignored if an SNI value is present in HTTPS requests.

destination-group-types.statement: Destination groups in an SSL/TLS inspection rule may be IP, FQDN or Wildcard FQDN groups; countries and custom categories configured in a destination group are ignored.

quotes: The supported group types are IP, FQDN, and Wildcard FQDN.
The countries and custom categories configured in the destination groups are ignored.

connect-user-agent-explicit-only.statement: The CONNECT User-Agent criterion applies only to SSL/TLS traffic forwarded in explicit proxy mode (PAC or PAC over tunnel); it does not apply to transparent proxy (tunnel) or Z-Tunnel 1.0 traffic, which has no user-agent context, so a rule scoped by user agent cannot match that traffic.
connect-user-agent-explicit-only.conditions: The consequence for rule matching (a user-agent-scoped rule cannot match transparent traffic) is read from 'Not applied'; the help page does not state the match outcome.

quotes: This criterion applies only to SSL/TLS traffic forwarded in explicit proxy mode (PAC or PAC over tunnel) and not to traffic forwarded via a transparent proxy (tunnel) or Z-Tunnel 1.0 due to lack of user agent context.

zpa-segments-sipa-only.statement: The ZPA Application Segment criterion lists only segments that have Source IP Anchor enabled (up to 255 selectable); in the API it is the `zpaAppSegments` list, documented as Source IP Anchoring-enabled segments.

quotes: The list displays only those Private Access application segments that have the Source IP Anchor option enabled.
Select up to 255 Private Access (ZPA) application segments.

expect.description: List of Source IP Anchoring-enabled ZPA Application Segments for which this rule is applicable

evidence.note: zpaAppSegments: 'List of Source IP Anchoring-enabled ZPA Application Segments for which this rule is applicable'

platforms-values.statement: `platforms` is a list of Client Connector device platform tokens: `SCAN_IOS`, `SCAN_ANDROID`, `SCAN_MACOS`, `SCAN_WINDOWS`, `SCAN_LINUX`, and `NO_CLIENT_CONNECTOR`. The SDKs declare it as a plain string list with no enum, so only the API contract and the Terraform provider restrict the values.

evidence.note: platforms enum: SCAN_IOS, SCAN_ANDROID, SCAN_MACOS, SCAN_WINDOWS, NO_CLIENT_CONNECTOR, SCAN_LINUX

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector device platforms for which the rule must be applied.
self.platforms = ZscalerCollection.form_list(config["platforms"] if "platforms" in config else [], str)
"SCAN_IOS", "SCAN_ANDROID", "SCAN_MACOS", "SCAN_WINDOWS", "NO_CLIENT_CONNECTOR", "SCAN_LINUX",

platforms-label-inferred.statement: The console most likely surfaces the platform criterion as Device Groups by OS type: the Leading Practices Guide writes rules as 'Device Group is Android, iOS, Windows, or macOS' and 'Device Group is No Client Connector', which matches the `platforms` tokens, so `NO_CLIENT_CONNECTOR` is the 'inspect Client Connector devices, exempt the rest' selector.
platforms-label-inferred.conditions: Inference: the guide never mentions the API field. The match between its OS-type Device Group wording and the `platforms` tokens is by content, not by any source that links them. The SSL/TLS rule page separately lists Device Groups and Devices as criteria with no OS field.

quotes: Device Groups (OS Type). You can only identify device groups if the traffic is forwarded to Zscaler via the Zscaler Client Connector.
Rule 1: Inspect if Cloud App is OneDrive or SharePoint, Device Group is Android, iOS, Windows, or macOS, and the Location is HQ.
Rule 4: Exempt if Device Group is No Client Connector for Location HQ.

road-warrior-kerberos.statement: `roadWarriorForKerberos` is the API form of the Remote Users with Kerberos criterion: when true the rule applies to remote users on PAC with Kerberos authentication, and it does not cover users forwarded by Client Connector.
road-warrior-kerberos.conditions: That the API field is the console's Remote Users with Kerberos criterion is inferred from matching wording; no source names the pair.

quotes: This criterion applies only to remote user traffic with Kerberos authentication, which is forwarded via PAC files and not via Zscaler Client Connector.

evidence.note: roadWarriorForKerberos: 'When set to true, the rule is applied to remote users that use PAC with Kerberos authentication.'

identity-needs-zcc-or-surrogate-ip.statement: User, Group and Department criteria work only when traffic arrives through Client Connector (preferred) or through GRE/IPsec with Enforce Surrogate IP; without either the service cannot identify the user before inspection to properly apply user-based policies. Device Group criteria need Client Connector.
identity-needs-zcc-or-surrogate-ip.conditions: 'Do not apply' is the guide's 'cannot identify the user ... to properly apply user-based policies'; the guide does not say whether the rule is skipped or evaluated as no match.

quotes: You can only use user attributes if the traffic forwarded to Zscaler is from the Zscaler Client Connector (preferred) or if you enable Enforce Surrogate IP
Without Zscaler Client Connector or Surrogate IP, the service cannot identify the user (before inspection) to properly apply user-based policies and determine if inspection is desired.

User Attributes (Group/Department). You can only use user attributes if the traffic forwarded to Zscaler is from the Zscaler Client Connector (preferred) or if you enable Enforce Surrogate IP and properly work for traffic flowing through GRE or IPSec tunnels to Zscaler.
Device Groups (OS Type). You can only identify device groups if the traffic is forwarded to Zscaler via the Zscaler Client Connector.

device-trust-scope.statement: Device Trust Level values High, Medium and Low apply only to Client Connector traffic; Unknown applies to all traffic.

quotes: While the High Trust, Medium Trust, or Low Trust evaluation is applicable only to Zscaler Client Connector traffic, Unknown evaluation applies to all traffic.

second-dimension-narrows.statement: Criteria in different groups of the match expression are ANDed, so adding a criterion from another group narrows a rule; only values inside a bracketed group widen it.
second-dimension-narrows.conditions: Applies to criteria that are set; an unset device-side criterion is ignored (zcc-criteria-unset-ignored) and so does not narrow.

absent-from-url-filtering-and-cac.title: Whether road_warrior_for_kerberos and zpaAppSegments are absent from URL Filtering and Cloud App Control rules
absent-from-url-filtering-and-cac.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Not available on URL Filtering or CAC rules - SSL-inspection-specific' and 'Absent from URL Filtering and CAC rules'. This is an absence claim; it would be settled by searching the URL Filtering and Cloud App Control rule schemas for the two fields.

platforms-console-label.title: What the console calls the SSL rule `platforms` (OS) criterion
platforms-console-label.detail: The rule-page criteria list names Device Groups and Devices only. The Leading Practices Guide describes Device Group selections by OS and 'No Client Connector', which fits `platforms`, but no capture shows the console control itself.

ip-dest-group-ignored-effect.title: What an SSL rule scoped only by IP destination groups does when the request carries SNI
ip-dest-group-ignored-effect.detail: The rule page says IP address-based destination groups are ignored when an SNI value is present. It does not say whether the rule then matches as if the criterion were unset (every SNI request) or does not match (only requests without SNI).
